content: Cedax, also known as cefditoren, is an antibiotic medication. Each capsule contains 400 mg of the active ingredient cefditoren. Indications: Cedax is effective against a range of bacterial pathogens, including Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Klebsiella oxytoca, Proteus vulgaris, Proteus mirabilis, Providencia species, Salmonella species, Shigella species, Enterobacter species, and Streptococcus species. It is indicated for the treatment of acute bronchitis, pneumonia, urinary tract infections, enteritis, and gastroenteritis. Dosage: The recommended duration of treatment is 5 to 10 days. For adults, the standard dose is 400 mg per day. For children, the dosage is 9 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, with a maximum dose of 400 mg. Cedax is most effective when taken on an empty stomach, either at least one hour before a meal or at least two hours after a meal. Adverse Reactions: In clinical studies involving 3,000 patients, Cedax was generally well-tolerated. The most commonly reported side effects were gastrointestinal disturbances and nausea. Warnings: Cedax should be prescribed with extreme caution in individuals who have a known allergy to penicillins.
